[USER] User is considering upgrading from a Fender Stratocaster to a Gibson Les Paul.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The main differences between Fender Stratocaster and Gibson Les Paul include:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] **Body Shape and Construction**: Stratocaster has a contoured, beveled body with a bolt-on neck, made of alder, ash, or mahogany; Les Paul has a single-cutaway, mahogany body with a set-in neck, made of mahogany with a carved maple top.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] **Neck and Fingerboard**: Stratocaster has a bolt-on neck, typically made of maple, with a 25.5" scale length and a 22-fret fingerboard; Les Paul has a set-in neck, made of mahogany, with a 24.75" scale length and a 22-fret fingerboard.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] **Electronics**: Stratocaster has three single-coil pickups with a 5-way switch, master volume, and tone controls; Les Paul has two humbucker pickups with a 3-way toggle switch, individual volume and tone controls for each pickup.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] **Tone**: Stratocaster is brighter, snappier, and more articulate; Les Paul is warmer, fuller, and has more sustain.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] **Playability**: Stratocaster is known for its comfortable, contoured body and fast, slim neck profile; Les Paul has a thicker neck profile and a more angular body shape.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] **Weight**: Stratocaster is typically lighter, around 7-8 pounds; Les Paul is typically heavier, around 9-10 pounds.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] **Price**: Stratocaster generally starts around $600-$800 for an American-made model; Les Paul generally starts around $1,000-$1,500 for an American-made model.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] If the user plays clean, crisp rhythms and leads, the Stratocaster might be better; if they play heavier music or prefer a warmer tone, the Les Paul might be better.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] It's a good idea to try out both guitars before making a purchase.
